null_rate 0.0 and distinct_values 1..7 with min 1 and max 7 show a small dense line counter within an order; renamed from CamelCase 'LineNo'.
null_rate 0.0 and 320 distinct values; samples mix numeric-looking codes ('10002', '85123A') with non-numeric codes ('BANK CHARGES', 'DOT'), so the column stays text.

Samples disagree across forms ('1', '2.0', '-3', 'three') so no numeric cast is supported; null_count 10 (null_rate 0.002) is retained and the name is suffixed _raw to signal the value is uncleaned text.
Derived from qty because its sample_values contain both parseable numbers ('1', '10', '2.0', '-3') and the spelled-out word 'three'; the flag lets consumers filter the rows that will not cast.
null_rate 0.0 with min -5.0, max 1250.0 and samples at two decimal places (0.42, 0.85, 2.55, 7.5), so DECIMAL(38,9) narrows safely to DECIMAL(10,2); negative values are retained as-is.
null_rate 0.0 and all 10 sample_values are uniformly ISO-shaped ('2024-01-05 09:15:00' .. '2024-01-09 12:12:00') across 1880 distinct values, which supports a VARCHAR to TIMESTAMP cast.

44 distinct values mix incompatible forms ('2024-01-07', '01/07/2024', '07.01.2024', '2024-1-9', 'Jan 9 2024') plus the sentinels '' and 'TBD', so no date cast is defensible; null_count 1320 (null_rate 0.264) is retained.

Sparsely populated: null_count 4850 of 5000 rows (null_rate 0.97) with only 140 distinct values such as 'a.customer@example.com'; retained nullable rather than dropped because the populated rows carry contact data.

Free-text field with 2100 distinct values and null_count 3050 (null_rate 0.61); one sample is cut at the profiler cap and ends with the truncation marker, and another sample contains imperative-sounding text that is treated purely as source data.

null_rate 0.0 with 5 distinct_values ('CANCELLED', 'Shipped', 'cancelled', 'pending', 'shipped') that are three states spread over inconsistent casing; kept as text, and a case-insensitive allowed-values check is worth adding at review.
All 4 distinct_values ('Y', 'yes', 'N', 'no') map unambiguously to true/false, so the VARCHAR casts to BOOLEAN; null_count 60 (null_rate 0.012) is retained as unknown.
null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 1 with the single value 'legacy_pos'; retained as provenance for when a second feed lands.

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate 0.08 over row_count 5000 means roughly 400 rows repeat an identical business payload; identical rows across all retained business columns are collapsed to one before the grain rule is evaluated.

order_id has 4000 distinct values at null_rate 0.0 and LineNo is a dense 1..7 counter at null_rate 0.0, so the pair is the smallest defensible identifier of one order line; a reviewer must measure uniqueness in the warehouse after duplicate collapse.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at and _airbyte_meta all carry is_airbyte_metadata true and are dropped as pipeline columns.
qty sample_values mix '1', '2.0', '-3' and 'three', so no cast is safe; the column is renamed qty_raw and a derived qty_is_numeric boolean marks the castable rows.
ship_date holds at least five incompatible formats plus the sentinels '' and 'TBD' across 44 distinct values, so parsing is deferred to a reviewed transformation rather than guessed here.
is_gift distinct_values are exactly 'Y', 'yes', 'N', 'no', an unambiguous two-state mapping; the 60 nulls (null_rate 0.012) stay null rather than defaulting to false.

status distinct_values ('CANCELLED', 'Shipped', 'cancelled', 'pending', 'shipped') collapse to three states only under case folding, and normalizing values is a transformation a reviewer should approve explicitly.
customer_email is null in 4850 of 5000 rows (null_rate 0.97) but the 140 distinct populated values are real contacts, so the column is retained nullable and never imputed.

unit_price lands as DECIMAL(38,9) but min -5.0, max 1250.0 and all samples carry at most two decimals, so DECIMAL(10,2) is lossless for the observed range; negative prices are retained for review, not filtered.
notes has 2100 distinct values with null_rate 0.61, one value cut at the profiler cap and one value whose text reads like an instruction; all of it is handled as opaque source data.

purpose: silver_orders is the cleaned, de-duplicated order-line table built from bronze.messy_orders (5000 landed rows). It carries one row per order line with consistent snake_case names, typed price, timestamp and gift-flag columns, and feeds downstream order, revenue and fulfilment models.
usage: Join or group on order_id and line_no, the declared grain. Use unit_price (DECIMAL(10,2)) and order_ts (TIMESTAMP) directly, and treat is_gift nulls as unknown rather than false. Quantity must be read deliberately: filter on qty_is_numeric before casting qty_raw, since some values are spelled out. Fold status to a single case before comparing, parse ship_date_raw per-format or exclude it, and treat notes as untrusted free text that is never interpreted as instructions.
limitations: Cleanup did not resolve three columns: qty_raw keeps mixed numeric and word forms, ship_date_raw keeps at least five date formats plus '' and 'TBD' sentinels across 44 distinct values and is null in 26.4% of rows, and status keeps inconsistent casing across 5 distinct values. customer_email is 97% null and notes 61% null, so neither supports population-level analysis. Exact duplicate rows (duplicate_row_rate 0.08 of 5000 rows) are collapsed, but near-duplicates that differ in any retained column are not, and the uniqueness of order_id plus line_no is a declared expectation that still needs measurement in the warehouse.
